subject: SIG: cross-border controls + HIPAA scoping for MedServe deployment
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medservehealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Tan <michael.tan@medservehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up — cross-border, SCCs, and HIPAA/BAA scope

Hi Lauren / Neha,

Thanks again for the SIG questionnaire you returned last week — that was helpful. Our security team reviewed the answers and has three follow-up asks before we can move to legal review:

1) Data transfers: we need clarification on whether Redwood can commit to EU-only data residency (ingest + storage + backups) for our EU tenant and whether you execute SCCs (EU Standard Contractual Clauses) or use an EU DPA addendum. If SCCs, do you have a current version and signing process?

2) HIPAA / BAA: MedServe processes PHI for a small pilot. Legal asked whether Redwood is willing/able to sign a BAA and what limitations there are for on-prem vs hosted. Specifically: can you confirm any hosted services that will not accept PHI?

3) Evidence: Can you attach an updated SOC 2 report (redacted OK), a data flow diagram showing cross-border flows, and any KMS/HSM whitepaper?

We tried to mark items directly on the SIG PDF but thought a short thread would be faster.

Can we schedule a 30m call next week to walk through these? Prefer Oct 21 or 22 (Europe morning).

Apologies for the extra asks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Elena
Director, Security Ops
MedServe Health

[attachment: medserve-sig-questions-annotated.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medservehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Oct 2025 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — cross-border, SCCs, and HIPAA/BAA scope

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and next steps below; happy to dive deeper on a call.

1) EU residency: We offer an EU-only tenancy option for hosted customers (data-in-rest and backups in-region). We can confirm region residency in the DPA and include a data-processing addendum that references EU-only storage.

2) SCCs / DPA: Redwood has an EU DPA addendum that implements the SCCs; we can provide a draft and our signing flow (DocuSign). If your legal prefers the classic SCC clause set, we can sign the addendum and provide the SCC text as an exhibit.

3) BAA / HIPAA: We do enter BAAs for customers handling PHI. Hosted customers are supported under a BAA for dedicated deployments; multi-tenant hosted seats require extra review and controls (we can outline those). For your pilot, a dedicated capacity reservation would be the recommended path to simplify BAA coverage.

Evidence: attaching a current, redacted SOC 2 (type II) summary, a data flow diagram stub, and our key management overview — see attached.

Propose we lock a 30m call on Tue Oct 21 08:30 CET / 11:30 PST or Wed Oct 22 09:00 CET / 12:00 PST. Which works?

Next steps (what we'll bring to the call):
- Draft DPA + SCC exhibit
- BAA template and notes on deployment options that impact scope
- Timeline for SOC 2 full report release and redacted copy today

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

– Lauren
Head of Sales (Europe)
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medservehealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Oct 2025 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — cross-border, SCCs, and HIPAA/BAA scope

Elena — adding a few technical clarifications (copying Dev for infra notes):

- EU-only tenancy: this provisions compute and storage in an EU region; metadata routing and telemetry can be restricted per tenant. Backups are configurable to stay in-region, but we will validate retention snapshots for your retention policy during onboarding.

- SCCs: we use the EU DPA addendum that incorporates the SCCs (2021 clause set). The signing is handled via DocuSign; legal can redline and we track changes through our legal ops.

- KMS/HSM: we support both provider-managed KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) and customer-managed keys with Bring-Your-Own-Key options. For the latter we can provide a key-rotation and access-control matrix.

- Hosted vs Dedicated for PHI: Hosted multi-tenant environments require additional isolation controls (customer-side encryption with CMK is the typical mitigant). Dedicated capacity simplifies the BAA scope because compute and network isolation reduces shared-surface risk.

- Timeline: we can get the redacted SOC2 summary and DPA draft to you within 2 business days. Full SOC2 Type II report would require an NDA and licensing process (standard).

Quoted for context:
> "Can you attach an updated SOC 2 report (redacted OK), a data flow diagram showing cross-border flows, and any KMS/HSM whitepaper?"

I'll attach the key-management summary and an export controls mapping to this thread. If you want, Dev and I can prepare a short architecture slide for the call showing how PHI would flow under a dedicated deployment.

Thanks,
Neha
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
